children: Proxy advisory firm Glass Lewis has recommended that Ethan Allen

shareholders support activist investor Doug Bergeron's campaign to replace all five directors, including longtime Chief Executive Farooq Kathwari, intensifying a boardroom battle ahead of the furniture maker's Nov. 4 annual meeting.
Bergeron and his investment firm, DGB Investments, own 5.2% of Ethan Allen

, which has a market capitalization of approximately $515 million. Glass Lewis endorsed all five of the activist's nominees, citing concerns about deteriorating operating performance, weak shareholder returns and insufficient board accountability, Reuters reported Sunday.
For investors, the endorsement increases pressure on Ethan Allen's

leadership and could improve Bergeron's chances of gaining control of the board. The company's shares have fallen more than 25% over the past year, closing Friday at $20.45. Bergeron argues that his proposed strategic and operational changes could potentially triple shareholder value within three years, although achieving that target remains uncertain.

Glass Lewis is the second proxy advisory firm to support Bergeron's entire slate, following a similar recommendation from Egan-Jones Proxy Services last week. Institutional Shareholder Services, another influential adviser to institutional investors, has yet to issue its recommendation. Bergeron's nominees bring experience in furniture retailing, corporate turnarounds, luxury retail and digital strategy.
The campaign also centers on succession planning for Kathwari, 82, who has led Ethan Allen

for 38 years. The company has pledged to appoint a successor by June 30, 2027, while retaining Kathwari as chief executive during the transition and as a director until its 2027 annual meeting. Bergeron has criticized the succession plan as overdue, arguing that more immediate leadership changes are needed to reverse the company's prolonged underperformance.

title: Glass Lewis backs activist's bid to replace entire Ethan Allen board
